title: Taifa of Almería
capsule: The Taifa of Almería emerged around 1012–1015 during the disintegration of the Umayyad Caliphate of Córdoba, becoming one of roughly two dozen petty Muslim kingdoms (taifas) that divided al-Andalus. Under the Khayranid and later the Banu Sumadih dynasty, Almería became a prosperous maritime and silk-trading port and a center of Andalusi high culture; al-Mu'tasim ibn Sumadih (d. 1091) hosted poets including Ibn Khafaja and maintained a celebrated garden palace, the Alcazaba. The taifa was absorbed by the Almoravids in 1091, briefly revived as a second taifa (c. 1145–1147) and a third taifa under Almohad decline before definitively falling to Castile in 1489.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The taifa's core territory around Almería is documented, but the extent of its fluctuating coastal and inland hinterlands across multiple taifa periods is imprecisely mapped.
